toolLimitation.reason: WALA models explicit reflective calls to ClassLoader.loadClass() and Class.forName() when they appear as invocations in application code with string constant arguments (handled by ClassFactoryContextSelector). However, WALA does not model the implicit ClassLoader.loadClass() calls that the JVM internally makes when executing 'new' bytecode instructions to ensure the target class is loaded before instantiation. The visitNew method in SSAPropagationCallGraphBuilder processes the allocation, creates instance keys, and calls processClassInitializer to handle <clinit> methods, but treats the JVM's internal class loading mechanism as outside the application call graph's scope.

potentialTestCase.description: Create a Java program with a class containing a static initializer that instantiates another class via 'new'. The static initializer executes when the class is loaded. At runtime, when the JVM executes the 'new' instruction for the second class, it implicitly calls ClassLoader.loadClass() to load that class before instantiation. WALA's call graph will include the edge from <clinit> to the constructor of the instantiated class, but will not include the edge from <clinit> to ClassLoader.loadClass(). Example: class App { static Helper h = new Helper(); public static void main(String[] args) {} } class Helper {}. The missed edge is App.<clinit>() → ClassLoader.loadClass("Helper").
